        - text: "UK product information also lists hair loss: 2.5% on Wegovy and 4.9% on Mounjaro in the weight-management trials, against 1.0% on placebo."

      - term: United Arab Emirates
      - definition:
        - text: In the UAE, the Emirates Drug Establishment (EDE) announced on 1 June 2026 that it had approved oral Wegovy (semaglutide) for long-term weight management in adults with obesity, or overweight with weight-related conditions, and a Ministry of Health and Prevention alert (Circular 9217/2024, October 2024) described genuine Mounjaro as registered for type 2 diabetes and weight management. Federal Decree-Law 38/2024 bars compounding pharmacies from compounding essential copies of products that hold an EDE marketing approval unless no commercially available product can deliver the expected benefit to the patient. On 20 July 2026 the EDE warned that 1,659 packs of Mounjaro and Ozempic missing from a warehouse are outside the legitimate supply chain and told the public to buy these medicines only from licensed pharmacies.
        - generic: "Source: Emirates Drug Establishment approves oral Wegovy® (semaglutide) for weight management and cardiovascular risk reduction · MOHAP Circular No. (9217)/2024: Alert Against the use of Counterfeit version of medicinal product (Mounjaro) · Federal Decree-Law No. (38) of 2024 Governing Medical Products, Pharmacists and Pharmaceutical Establishments (official English translation) · EDE Circular No. (31/2026): Awareness Circular – Stolen Packs of Mounjaro® and Ozempic®"
      - term: Saudi Arabia
      - definition:
        - text: Saudi product information describes weight-management or diabetes indications, depending on brand. These are not skin-rejuvenation approvals. Sudden visual symptoms require urgent ophthalmological assessment. Current Saudi product-record and label verification for Mounjaro (tirzepatide) remains open in this edition; this does not mean it is banned or unregistered.
        - generic: "Source: SFDA-agreed semaglutide safety communication and Saudi indications"
    - paragraph: The phrase bundles four kinds of statement. Kept apart, they tell a patient far more than the headline does.
    - strong: Mechanism
    - generic: Volume loss
    - generic: Losing fat deflates the superficial facial compartments and unmasks laxity that was already there.
    - strong: Human evidence
    - generic: "Observational and small: C to D"
    - generic: One imaging study of 20 patients found a median 9% loss of midface volume, mostly superficial, about 7% per 10 kg lost. A survey of 1,226 patients found sagging, facial volume loss and hair shedding reported more often the more weight was lost. A systematic review of the plastic-surgery literature found it limited by study bias. No randomized trial has measured the face.
    - strong: Regulatory status (US, September 2026)
    - generic: Hair loss labelled; facial change unlisted
    - generic: Both labels list hair loss (about 3–6% on drug against about 1% on placebo, mostly in women, linked to weight reduction). The semaglutide label also lists altered skin sensation. Facial volume loss is not a labelled adverse reaction.
    - strong: Open question
    - generic: A direct drug effect?
    - generic: Whether these drugs act on facial fat or skin cells beyond the effect of weight loss rests on cell studies and has not been tested in people.
    - paragraph: So far, the evidence ties facial change to how much weight is lost.
